name.what: The name the team knows the system that sends the invoices by, for example Waiter.
name.where: You choose it. It shows in notices, the log and reports.

webhook.what: The https address where Fiscal. tells that system every state change of a document (validated, rejected, in contingency). Notices are signed.
webhook.where: The client system's technical team gives it to you. You can leave it empty and set it later on the client system's page.

secret.what: The key the client system signs its calls to Fiscal. with. It goes with the key identifier.
secret.where: Fiscal. shows it only once: when the client system is created or the secret is rotated.
secret.secret: Keep it in a password manager and hand it to the technical team over a safe channel. Never by chat or e-mail.

grace.what: Hours the previous secret keeps working, so the client system can switch without an outage.
grace.where: 24 hours is usually enough. 0 stops it now: use it if the secret was exposed.

nit.what: The business's tax identification number. For a natural person it is their ID number.
nit.where: RUT, box 5. Without the check digit.

dv.what: The last digit of the NIT, computed by the DIAN.
dv.where: RUT, box 6. Fiscal. computes it from the NIT; if it does not match the RUT, check the NIT.

personType.what: Whether the business is a company (legal person) or a person (natural person).
personType.where: RUT, box 24: 1 is a legal person and 2 a natural person.

legalName.what: The business's legal name, exactly as in the RUT. It goes on every invoice.
legalName.where: RUT, box 35 (company name) or boxes 31 to 34 (a natural person's names).

tradeName.what: The business's trade name, if it differs from the legal one.

responsibilities.what: The business's tax obligations. If they do not match the RUT, the DIAN rejects the invoices (rule FAJ26).
responsibilities.where: RUT, box 53: 13 is O-13, 15 is O-15, 23 is O-23 and 47 is O-47. If none applies, «Not applicable» (R-99-PN). When in doubt, ask the accountant.

taxScheme.what: The main tax the business charges on its sales: VAT, national consumption tax (INC) or none.
taxScheme.where: RUT, box 53: 48 is VAT; 33 is INC (common in restaurants); 49 «Not VAT liable» is «Not applicable». The accountant confirms it.

address.what: The business's main address. It goes on the invoices.

municipality.what: The municipality of the address. Fiscal. stores its DANE code, which the DIAN asks for.
municipality.where: RUT, box 40. Type the name and pick it from the list.

email.what: The business's e-mail shown on the invoices.
email.where: RUT, box 42, or whichever the business prefers for invoicing.

phone.what: A contact phone that goes on the invoices.

kind.what: Entities deliver the certificate in two ways: one password-protected file (.p12 or .pfx), or the certificate and the private key as separate files.
kind.where: Check the e-mail or the portal of the entity that issued it.

file.what: The business's digital signature certificate. Fiscal. signs every invoice with it. It is issued by an entity accredited by ONAC.
file.where: The business downloads it from its certification entity's portal. It must be a file, not a USB token.

password.what: The password that protects the .p12 or .pfx file.
password.where: The business sets it when downloading the certificate, or the entity sends it.
password.secret: Type it yourself right here. Fiscal. uses it once to open the file and keeps the certificate encrypted.

keyFile.what: The private key that goes with the certificate (.key). Nothing can be signed without it.
keyFile.where: The entity delivers it with the certificate, or it was generated on the computer when requesting it.
keyFile.secret: It is the secret part of the certificate: do not e-mail it or upload it anywhere else.

environment.what: Habilitación is the DIAN's test environment, with no tax effect. Production is the real one.
environment.where: Until the DIAN accepts the test set, it stays in habilitación.

softwareId.what: The identifier the DIAN gives Fiscal. inside this business's registration. It is not secret.
softwareId.where: Habilitation portal → Registro y habilitación → Documentos electrónicos → Factura electrónica → Configurar modos de operación → «Software propio» row, ID column. It is also on the test set page.

pin.what: The PIN the business chose when it associated Fiscal. as its own software. It goes in the security code of every document.
pin.where: The business typed it in the «Pin del SW» field of «Configurar modos de operación».
pin.secret: It is secret: type it yourself, never in a chat, e-mail or ticket. The portal shows it on screen, so do not share your screen on those pages.

testSetId.what: The identifier of the test set the DIAN assigned to this registration. It is not secret.
testSetId.where: Habilitation portal → list of operation modes → Fiscal.'s row, «Acciones» column → «¡Importante!» notice at the top of the test set page.

resolution.what: The number of the DIAN resolution that authorizes this numbering.
resolution.where: Habilitación: test set page → «Rango de numeración asignado» (18760000001). Production: the resolution issued in MUISCA.

prefix.what: The letters before the invoice number, like SETP in SETP990000001. Up to 4 characters.
prefix.where: On the same resolution or test set page. In habilitación it is SETP.

numbers.what: The first and last numbers authorized in the range.
numbers.where: On the resolution or the test set page. Habilitación: 990000000 to 995000000.

validity.what: The dates between which the resolution allows invoicing with this range.
validity.where: On the resolution or the test set page. Habilitación: 2019-01-19 to 2030-01-19.

technicalKey.what: The 40-character key of this range. Fiscal. uses it to compute each invoice's CUFE; if it is wrong, the DIAN rejects with FAD06.
technicalKey.where: Habilitación: test set page → «Información del software» (click the field, Ctrl+A and Ctrl+C). Production: Fiscal. fetches it with «Fetch the numbering from the DIAN».
technicalKey.secret: It is secret: copy it straight from the portal into this field. Never paste it in a chat.

kind.what: Invoicing: the numbering authorized for electronic invoices. Contingency: the paper booklet (type 03) for when there is no system.
kind.where: The DIAN authorizes both by resolution.

resolutionDate.what: The date the DIAN issued the resolution.

establishment.what: The branch or till that uses this range.
establishment.where: If the business has several branches, each one has its prefix in the resolution.

size.what: How many invoices, credit notes and debit notes the DIAN asks for to accept the set.
size.where: Test set page in the portal → «Total de documentos requeridos». The usual one is 30, 10 and 10.

habilitado.what: The last step of the habilitation portal: the business sets the date it starts invoicing electronically.
habilitado.where: The business marks it in the portal after talking to its accountant. It is irreversible and adds responsibility 52 to the RUT.

numbering.what: Production numbering is authorized by a DIAN resolution, and its prefix is associated with Fiscal. before fetching it.
numbering.where: DIAN online services (MUISCA) → invoicing numbering request. Then, in the production e-invoicing portal, the prefix is associated with the software.

letter.what: The draft letter the business uses to tell the DIAN about the invoices it made in contingency in a period.
letter.where: Fiscal. builds it from the contingencies of the chosen dates. The legal representative signs it and the business sends it to contingencia.facturadorvp@dian.gov.co.

role.what: Operator: sees and runs documents, issuers, contingencies and alerts. Administrator: also invites users, rotates secrets, switches issuers and ranges on or off and moves issuers to production.
role.where: Choose it by what the person needs to do. It can be changed later.

helpPage.title: Guides and help
helpPage.subtitle: Each process, step by step, to do it alone or with Claude in Chrome.
helpPage.howTitle: How to use a guide with Claude in Chrome

howSteps.1: Open the portal or the Fiscal. page you will work on.
howSteps.2: Copy the guide with «Copy guide», paste it into Claude in Chrome and type «let's start».
howSteps.3: Claude tells you what to do and fills in the data that is not secret. You sign in, pick the files and type the PIN, technical key and passwords.
howSteps.4: Before every irreversible step, Claude stops and asks for confirmation. At the end it gives you a summary without secrets.

helpPage.safetyTitle: What you never give to Claude or anyone
helpPage.safetyBody: The software PIN, the technical key, the certificate password, a client system's secret and the DIAN tokens. The guides tell Claude so; if a screen shows them, copy them yourself.
helpPage.tipsBody: Next to the fields that ask for DIAN, RUT or certificate data there is a «?» that explains what the data is and where it comes from.
